did_you_know.text: Did you know? Elisha prophesied that within a single day there would be a dramatic change: at the gate of Samaria, a seah of fine flour would sell for one shekel and two seahs of barley for one shekel, even though the city was suffering from famine and under siege.

Did you know? The royal officer, who was close to the king and leaned on his arm, doubted Elisha’s prophecy. Elisha replied that he would see the abundance with his own eyes, but would not be able to eat any of it.

Did you know? Four lepers were sitting outside the city gate. Rather than wait for death, they decided to act: if they entered the city, they would die of hunger, but if they went to the Aramean camp, they might live.

Did you know? According to the account, the LORD caused the Arameans to hear the sound of a large army, so they thought the king of Israel had hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack them.

Did you know? After discovering that the camp was deserted, the lepers ate and drank, then took silver, gold, and clothing and hid them. After doing this twice, they realized that they had to report the news to the city.
Did you know? The lepers described their discovery of the camp as “a day of good news” and realized that delaying the news until morning might be counted against them as wrongdoing.

Did you know? The king feared that the Arameans had left the camp as part of an ambush, but one of his servants suggested sending riders to investigate the area using the horses that remained in the city.

Did you know? The messengers found clothing and equipment scattered along the road all the way to the Jordan, which the Arameans had thrown away in their haste as they fled. This strengthened the belief that the camp had truly been abandoned.
Did you know? After the people plundered the Aramean camp, grain prices fell exactly as Elisha had prophesied: a seah of fine flour for one shekel and two seahs of barley for one shekel.
Did you know? The royal officer’s fate was exactly as Elisha had said: he saw the abundance at the gate, but the people trampled him there, and he died without eating any of it.
